newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Kvaerner unit formalises AIOC oil pipeline deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner unit formalises AIOC oil pipeline deal.

text.p: The Azerbaijan International Operating Company (AIOC) formalised a deal on Thursday for a Kvaerner ASA unit to refurbish an oil pipeline to carry some of AIOC's crude oil output to world markets.
Kvaerner John Brown, which won a $275 million tender in July to carry out work on the pipeline, formally signed documents with AIOC officials.

AIOC, a consortium of western oil giants led by British Petroleum Co Plc and Norway's Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil), needs the pipeline to ship some of its planned output from its $8 billion project in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea.
Kvaerner John Brown will begin refurbishing the 900 km (558 mile) pipeline, which runs from the Azeri capital Baku to the Georgian port of Supsa, in early 1997.

"Work should commence here by the end of the first quarter of 1997, and we should be ready to deliver oil to Supsa by the end of 1998," AIOC First Vice-President John W. Hollis said before a signing ceremony in the Georgian capital Tbilisi.
The pipeline, when repairs are completed by the end of 1998, will have a capacity of five million tonnes a year.
"We were very pleased to have been selected after strong international competition for this job," said Kvaerner John Brown Managing Director Peter Marshall.
The pipeline, a Soviet-era relic with hundreds of breaches along its length, is not now operational.
Baku-Supsa is one of two routes that will handle AIOC's so-called "early" oil. The other route runs from Baku to Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
A third, larger pipeline is needed, probably to the Mediterranean, for AIOC and possibly Kazakh output.
